about: The five release gates of document 10 §7 and where each criterion stands. Checked by scripts/verify-acceptance.mjs: the criteria must be the specification's; a gate may be marked passed only when every criterion is met and the owner's decision is recorded; the criterion on critical defects is worked out from defects.json.

states.met: true today, with the evidence named
states.partly: part of it is true; the lines close the rest

gates.title: Design foundation
gates.needs: The owner's approval of the design on the hosted workspace (T-005). The two other open points are the agent's work.

criteria.evidence: Tokens, shell and the Reimagined theme the owner asked for (DL-017) are built and pinned by tests (`Unit/AdminDesignTokensTest.php`, `Feature/ThemeTokensTest.php`). The approval itself has not been given.
No screen shows the shared components and their states side by side.
Sidebar, top bar and phone drawer are built. On 17 November a browser opened 241 screens as four roles at 1366 px and at 390 px; none was wider than the window (`scripts/os-screens.mjs`).
Counted by tools on every screen: labels, names, one main heading, 24 px targets. No review by keyboard and by screen reader.

gates.title: Module readiness
gates.needs: Passed module by module. Each open module has its sheet in §4; the owner signs or returns it (T-171).

criteria.evidence: Documents 05 and 07 are the requirements, and the schema is 106 migrations that build an empty MySQL 8.4 in CI on every push. No module has had its requirements, its addresses and its schema approved as a set.

Unit and feature tests pass: 2,359 on 17 November, and the same suite on MySQL 8.4 in CI. In a browser both journeys and a crawl of every screen as four roles pass, by hand and, since 17 November, in CI on every push that touches the admin (`.github/workflows/vercel-livewire.yml`); which of the eleven flows of document 10 they press is in §3.

No admin address opens without a sign-in, and one role is checked against every address (`Feature/AdminRouteAccessTest.php`); the other roles are tested module by module (§4). The roles are the inherited eight, not yet the owner's matrix.

Ready for the catalogue only: 170 products, with a report that accounts for every row and every change (`docs/furniture-2030/catalogue/IMPORT-REPORT.md`). No other record has an importer. The old database holds little to move: on 17 November 1 lead, 1 client, no order, quotation or invoice.

gates.title: Puck readiness
gates.needs: The prototype of T-115. Not started; it is wave 10.

criteria.evidence: Not started. The Website Studio in the code is the HTML builder inherited from Interior; it is switched off.

criteria.text: Draft security, publish and rollback tested.

gates.title: Hostinger readiness
gates.needs: The owner's Hostinger details and the two SSH secrets entered in GitHub (T-006). Nothing on the host can be proven before that.

criteria.evidence: Verified away from the host: every migration from an empty database and the whole suite run on MySQL 8.4 in CI on every push (`.github/workflows/os-ci.yml`). Not verified on the account: its PHP version and extensions, MySQL or MariaDB.
Designed — one cron line calls the scheduler, two timed jobs drain the queue — and never run on the host.
The Laravel admin holds no real record yet, and no backup of it has been taken or restored.

The outside security check exists and passes for the hosted workspace on Vercel (`.github/workflows/vercel-live-check.yml`); it has not been pointed at Hostinger, and nothing has been measured against the plan's limits. Published advisories for the packages are asked of npm and Composer when a lock file changes and every week (`.github/workflows/audit.yml`); none that blocks is open.

gates.title: Production cutover
gates.needs: The owner changes the old dashboard's password (T-021): the one open critical defect. Then gate D, and the owner's written approval of each module's move (T-181).

criteria.evidence: Given in general on 17 November: the owner lifted the holds to start a production-ready deployment (DL-022). The move of each module is approved in writing on its sheet.
No snapshot has been taken for a move. What the old database held on 17 November was read and is written down: 148 sample products, 1 lead, 1 client, 1 user, no order, quotation, invoice or payment.

Each change of 17 November has its own way back: the undo in `deploy/supabase/2026-11-17-close-data-api.sql`, the rollback file `scripts/migrations/rollback/019_catalogue.rollback.sql`, the earlier deployment kept by Vercel. A written plan for going back after a module has moved does not exist.

Both sites are asked from outside after every merge, and a timer for every six hours is in the workflow (`.github/workflows/live-check-after-merge.yml`, `.github/workflows/vercel-live-check.yml`); a failure opens an issue, proved with issue #38 on 17 November. GitHub had not yet started the timer by the afternoon of 17 November. No error tracker, no runbook.
